title: Xalavier Nelson Jr - Procedural Generation for Dogs
speaker: Xalavier Nelson Jr
description:
This talk is from the 2020 virtual Roguelike Celebration:
https://roguelike.club/event2020.html

Xalavier Nelson Jr. is an award-winning narrative director and writer who has held leading roles on titles including Hypnospace Outlaw, Can Androids Pray, SkateBIRD, We Are The Caretakers, and many, many more. His current project is an absurdist first-person open world comedy adventure game called An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs, for a variety of reasons we can no longer remember.

In this talk he admits being incredibly intimidated by the idea of procedural generation and scary words like 'corpus', which kept him from exploring proc gen techniques as a creator. However, he explains how in the context of Dog Airport Game he eased into this design space, and how he's now using modular content principles in a very simple way to build an ever-changing world of stock photo dogs.

Find him on Twitter: https://twitter.com/WritNelson
Check out his Patreon! https://www.patreon.com/StrangeScaffold
An Airport For Aliens Currently Run By Dogs: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1246250/An_Airport_for_Aliens_Currently_Run_by_Dogs/

You can simulate entire civilizations and you can create conin -- continents worth

look at the two words; procedural and generation. Procedure meaning

as these much more complicated, deeply impressive examples that we see in games super often.
And the key to understanding the difference in design to use procedural generation which is a
fundamental design tool for any game creator is understanding how it differs from the typical
development approach. When you are looking at something like a dwarf fortress and you see the
utter scope of that world you think wow, procedural generation isn't for me
